inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL view uses ISNULL on an optional identifier before concatenating a fallback string, distinguishing missing values from present values inside a larger projection.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as a contact audit that projects ISNULL's integer predicate result, classifies NULL versus present values, and applies the same fallback before concatenation; source views, schema, identifiers, and strings are not copied.

fixture_notes: Contact 201 has a phone extension, contact 202 has a NULL extension, and contact 203 has an empty extension; ISNULL must distinguish only the NULL value while the fallback projection keeps the audit label deterministic.
determinism_notes: Contact IDs, names, extensions, and ordering are fixed; the report uses no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections.
setup: CREATE TABLE contact_extension_audit (contact_id INT PRIMARY KEY, contact_label VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, extension_code VARCHAR(16) NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT contact_id, contact_label, ISNULL(extension_code) AS extension_missing, CASE WHEN ISNULL(extension_code) = 1 THEN 'missing' ELSE 'present' END AS extension_state, CONCAT(contact_label, ':', IFNULL(extension_code, 'unassigned')) AS routing_label FROM contact_extension_audit ORDER BY contact_id

checks.sql: SELECT contact_id, contact_label, extension_code FROM contact_extension_audit ORDER BY contact_id
